security_spec.violation_condition: QEMU sets iotval2[1] (implicit write bit) unconditionally from the original transaction's R/W attribute for all implicit guest page faults, instead of setting it only when the G-stage write-permission check (gpte.W==0) caused the fault
security_spec.summary: iotval2[1] incorrectly reports implicit write on all G-stage faults (e.g., gpte.V==0, gpte.N==1, PBMT violations) instead of only on gpte.W==0 faults, causing guest kernel to misattribute fault cause

findings.finding: iotval2[1] (IW / Implicit Write bit) is never explicitly encoded. iotval2 is set to raw GPA (iotlb->translated_addr) at riscv_iommu_translate:1658-1659, leaking GPA address bit 1 as iotval2[1] instead of setting it to 1 only when the G-stage fault was caused by gpte.W==0 during a read-for-write implicit access. A guest hypervisor relying on iotval2[1] to distinguish implicit-write G-stage faults from explicit G-stage faults will receive incorrect fault attribution.
findings.snippet:
return (iotlb->perm & IOMMU_WO) ?
                (pass ? RISCV_IOMMU_FQ_CAUSE_WR_FAULT_VS :
                        RISCV_IOMMU_FQ_CAUSE_WR_FAULT_S) :
                (pass ? RISCV_IOMMU_FQ_CAUSE_RD_FAULT_VS :
                        RISCV_IOMMU_FQ_CAUSE_RD_FAULT_S);

findings.finding: Fault reporting passes iotlb->translated_addr directly as iotval2 without masking off bit 1 or encoding the IW (Implicit Write) indicator. Per RISC-V IOMMU spec, iotval2[1] must be 1 only when a G-stage write-permission check (gpte.W==0) caused the fault, and 0 otherwise. The current code preserves whatever GPA address bit 1 happens to be, making it indistinguishable from a properly encoded IW bit.
findings.snippet:
riscv_iommu_report_fault(s, ctx, ttype, fault, enable_pid,
                                 iotlb->iova, iotlb->translated_addr);

findings.finding: G-stage A/D bit checks (lines 454-457) use iotlb->perm which was overwritten at line 472 during S-stage completion to reflect the S-stage PTE permissions rather than the original transaction intent. For a nested translation where the S-stage PTE grants RW but D-bit is missing on the G-stage PTE, the fault cause is correctly WR_FAULT_VS. However, iotval2 is set to the S-stage derived GPA without the IW bit, so a guest hypervisor checking iotval2[1] cannot tell whether this was an implicit write (S-stage write → G-stage D-bit miss) vs. an explicit G-stage access.

The diff adds a cross-field validation check: when iohgatp.MODE is Bare (G-stage disabled), msiptp.MODE must be Off. Without this check, a guest could configure MSI page tables through an undefined GSCID context when G-stage translation is disabled, potentially routing MSI writes to arbitrary physical addresses. This check correctly returns false (DDT_MISCONFIGURED / cause=259), closing a privilege_escape vulnerability documented in analysis_smip.md.
